 At Jabalpur

 Shri Narendra Nikhare - Advocate for the appellant.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mrs. Nupur Dhamija - Dy. Govt. Advocate for respondent.
Heard on admission.
Appeal, being arguable, is admitted for hearing.
Heard on I.A. No.33170 of 2024, first application under Section 430 of BNSS for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

2. This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 09.12.2024 passed by 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Lakhnadon, District Seoni (M.P.) in S.T. No.24/2021 whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 376(1) and 456 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and 02 years respective with fine of Rs.10,000/- and Rs.1000/- respectively with default stipulations.
3.

entities.text: 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Lakhnadon, District Seoni (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that in the statement of P.W.2, husband of prosecutrix, he has categorically stated that when he reached home, he saw prosecutrix and the appellant were in compromising position.
As per his statement there was consensual relationship between the prosecutrix and appellant.
Both the prosecutrix and accused are 45 years of age.
In view of the statement of P.W.2, husband of prosecutrix, the prosecution story appears to be doubtful.
It is further 2 CRA-14066-2024 submitted that the prosecutrix sustained no injury on her person.
Though DNA report is positive but keeping in view the statement of P.W.2, it is a case of consent.
Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
It is also submitted that the present appellant is ready and willing to abide by any condition which may be imposed by the Court.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant is entitled to be given the benefit of suspension of sentence.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text:
6 . Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the statement of P.W.2 who has not been declare hostile by the prosecution and thus, his statement is binding upon the prosecution, it appears to be a case of consent, but without commenting on merits of the case,
I.A. No.33170 of 2024 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.70,000/- (Rupees Seventy thousand Only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.

The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 07.10.2025 and on subsequent dates given by the trial Court in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE mrs. mishra Gudda Urf Yogendra Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16389776/
